content:
jun: Heads-up — saw repeated saturation on the hosted GPU nodepool in us-west-2 last night. Multiple namespaces ended up waiting for nodes and we had a few job evictions. Anyone else see this?

alex: saw it in the metrics too, spike around 02:10 UTC. ephemeral pods couldn't land because node autoscale lagged + kube-scheduler binpacking favored existing pods.

maya: interesting — was that the bursty retrain jobs or normal inference traffic?

jun: looks like mix of both. retrain jobs from data-team and some customer-inference bursts. retention windows made autoscaler slow to add new nodes.

sam: can you paste the most recent node events/logs?

jun: here are the relevant commands I ran:

```
kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=hosted-gpu -o wide
kubectl describe node gpu-hosted-47
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep Pending
```

jun: events show long Pending -> FailedScheduling with "0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" and CA scaled up but new nodes were NotReady for ~2m.

alex: NotReady for 2m -> likely image pull or driver init timing on GPU nodes. Late-binding of GPU driver + nvidia device plugin can cause that.

maya: can we optimize boot image: bake drivers into AMI/container OS to reduce time-to-ready?

sam: that helps but pushes cost. alternative: keep a small buffer of warm spare nodes in hosted pool (minNodes=N) so scale up latency becomes less visible.

jun: cost tradeoff: warm spares increase idle GPU cost. but we also have SLA penalties for dedicated customers when their inference latency jumps.

infra-bot: FYI — alert rule fired: gpu_pool_saturation_us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T02:12:03Z (alert_id: GPUP001).

alex: proposal: two-pronged approach: 1) change autoscaler settings for hosted GPU pools to faster scale-up and lower scale-down aggressiveness; 2) introduce namespace annotation to prefer dedicated pools for heavy/latency-sensitive tenants.

maya: +1 on annotation. something like `redwood.io/prefer-dedicated: "true"` that admission webhook respects and schedules to dedicated nodepools via a mutating label on pod/namespace.

sam: caution: we need an override path for bursty legitimate hosted traffic — else dedicated pool owners might see noisy neighbors if everyone annotations flips. maybe annotate with expected_gpu_hours or priority class.

jun: also noticed network flaps on ENIs while new nodes joined — pod-to-pod connectivity misses for ~30s until routes propagated. that exacerbates NotReady symptoms.

alex: this is a cloud VPC route table propagation issue; late-binding ENI attach + CNI (we run calico) sometimes delays rules. We could pre-attach ENIs for warm nodes or use accelerated networking/ENI Multiqueue.

maya: shorter-term: tweak cluster-autoscaler flags: `--scale-up-delay=10s` (lower), `--max-total-unready-percentage=50` (increase tolerant), `--scan-interval=10s`. and `--expander=least-waste` so new node types chosen minimize empty GPUs.

sam: for dedicated pools: set `maxNodesPerPool` and `minNodes` per tenant profile. Add eviction window for best-effort pods with QoS BestEffort throttling. keep system reserved for cuda initialization.

jun: question: how do we prevent hosted tenants from being scheduled onto dedicated pools accidentally? we've had a mislabelled pool before.

alex: enforce with namespace isolation policy in admission controller: `namespace.spec.nodeSelector` + deny if namespace has `redwood.io/tenant=dedicated-owner` but pods lack `redwood.io/owner` label. Also add an infra pipeline check that rejects creating nodepool without `nodepool-type` tag.

maya: we should run a short canary: pick one small tenant, place them on dedicated pool with warm spare 1-2 nodes, instrument latency/cost. Run for 72h.

sam: agree. measure GPU utilization, pod startup time, and new-node join latency. we need dashboard panels: `gpu_ready_time`, `node_init_time`, `pod_pending_duration`.

jun: I'll spin up the canary tonight in us-west-2. Steps: create dedicated nodepool with minNodes=1, maxNodes=8, taint `dedicated=true:NoSchedule`, add mutating webhook to copy namespace annotation to pod tolerations, and set autoscaler flags on that pool.

alex: remember quota/cost approvals. ping finance for temporary charge.

infra-bot: action created: infra/GPUP-canary-042 — assignees: jun, maya. due: 2026-03-18T12:00:00Z.

maya: also add a small change to node bootstrap: pre-pull critical images and enable driver pre-init script so node Ready occurs faster. I can PR the cloud-init today.

sam: after canary, we should consider a policy: tenants with sustained 95th percentile GPU usage > X% over 24h get auto-suggested migration to dedicated with cost estimate and opt-in. automate with Optimize toolkit.

jun: perfect — will post canary results and timeline. thanks all :rocket:
